Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray shows complete opacification of the left hemithorax with a mediastinal shift toward the left side, which is characteristic of volume loss (atelectasis/collapse) rather than a space-occupying lesion like a large pleural effusion that would push the mediastinum to the right. The accompanying CT confirms a collapsed left lung with an obstructing mass, consistent with tumor obstruction causing lobar collapse.
